subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Wildfire-Resistant Construction: Engineering Against Fire
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Wildfire-Resistant Construction: Engineering Against Fire.

hook.text: In the 2018 Camp Fire, houses with metal roofs and concrete walls survived while neighboring wood-frame homes burned down.

buildup.text: Embers travel up to a mile ahead of a wildfire. They enter through vents, gaps, and open windows — not just direct flame.

discovery.text: Fire-resistant zones — defensible space — reduce ignition risk. Clearing vegetation 30 feet from the structure is the minimum.

twist.text: Building codes in fire-prone areas lag behind the science. Some communities resist rules that increase construction costs.

climax.text: Australia's BAL system rates bushfire exposure and mandates matching standards. Extreme-zone homes use steel and concrete only.

punchline.text: Embers travel a mile. Vents let them in. Materials decide the outcome.

quiz.question: How do wildfires most commonly ignite homes ahead of the main fire front?
options: Radiant heat from the fire front melts vinyl siding from several hundred feet away
Embers travel up to a mile and enter through vents, gaps, and openings
Underground root fires emerge beneath the house foundation and ignite the floor
